description:
About the Position

Aarhus University invites applications for a PhD position on tracking microbes across borders using genomics to uncover biomass-to-biogas transmission pathways. The project applies genomic and bioinformatic methods to understand how microbial communities move through biomass supply chains and biogas plants, connecting findings to process performance in the bioenergy sector. The position is embedded in the university's research on green transition technologies and circular bioeconomy systems.

The successful candidate will combine field sampling, sequencing data generation and computational analysis to trace microbial populations across national borders and industrial sites. The work connects molecular microbiology with engineering practice, and findings will feed into improved inoculation, monitoring and risk-management strategies for biogas production. The PhD is a salaried three-year position under the Danish collective agreement, based at the Aarhus campus with project-related travel.

Project Approach

The project builds on genome-resolved metagenomics and comparative genomics to identify microbial strains, follow their transmission routes and relate them to biogas process outcomes. The candidate will develop analysis pipelines, work with industrial and research partners, and publish findings in international journals. Applicants should hold a master's degree in microbiology, bioinformatics, environmental engineering or a related discipline, and demonstrate skills in genomics data analysis; experience with anaerobic digestion or bioprocess engineering is an advantage.

Highlights

  • Genome-resolved metagenomics of microbial communities
  • Transmission pathway analysis across borders and sites
  • Biomass-to-biogas process microbiology
  • Bioinformatics pipeline development
  • Collaboration with bioenergy industry partners
  • Salaried three-year PhD under the Danish collective agreement
